verses.sanskrit:
अपरोक्षानुभूतिः।।
श्रीहरिं परमानन्दमुपदेष्टारमीश्वरम्।
व्यापकं सर्वलोकानां कारणं तं नमाम्यहम्।।1।।
verses.roman:
Aparokṣānubhūtiḥ
Śrīhariṃ paramānandamupadeṣṭāramīśvaram.
Vyāpakaṃ sarvalokānāṃ kāraṇaṃ taṃ namāmyaham..1..
verses.colloquial:
Aparokshaanubhuutih
shriiharim paramaanandam upadeshtaaram iishvaram.
Vyaapakam sarva lokaanaam kaaranam tam namaami aham ..1..
verses.translation_reworded: I bow to Sri Hari, the remover of ignorance, who is the Supreme Bliss, the First Teacher, Ishwara, the One who pervades everything, and the source of all Lokas (the universe).

verses.sanskrit:
अपरोक्षानुभूतिर्वै प्रोच्यते मोक्षसिद्धये।
सद्भिरेषा प्रयत्नेन वीक्षणीया मुहुर्मुहुः।।2।।
verses.roman:
Aparokṣānubhūtirvai procyate mokṣasiddhaye.
Sadbhireṣā prayatnena vīkṣaṇīyā muhurmuhuḥ..2..
verses.colloquial:
Aparoksha anubhuutir vai prochyate moksha siddhaye.
Sadbhi reshaa prayatnena viikshaniiyaa muhur muhuh ..2..
verses.translation_reworded: This work sets out the means of reaching Aparokshanubhuti (Self-Realization), so that final liberation may be gained. Only those who are pure in heart should meditate on the truth taught here, constantly and with all their effort.

verses.sanskrit:
स्ववर्णाश्रमधर्मेण तपसा हरितोषणात्।
साधनं प्रभवेत्पुंसां वैराग्यादिचतुष्टयम्।।3।।
verses.roman:
Svavarṇāśramadharmeṇa tapasā haritoṣaṇāt.
Sādhanaṃ prabhavetpuṃsāṃ vairāgyādicatuṣṭayam..3..
verses.colloquial:
Svavarna aashrama dharmena tapasaa haritoshanaat.
Saadhanam prabhavet pumsaam vairaagya aadi chatushtayam ..3..
verses.translation_reworded: People gain the four preliminary qualifications for knowledge, beginning with Vairagya (dispassion), by pleasing Hari (the Lord) through austerities and through carrying out the duties of their social order and stage of life.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तेषु वैराग्यं विषयेष्वनु।
यथैव काकविष्ठायां वैराग्यं तद्धि निर्मलम्।।4।।
verses.roman:
Brahmādisthāvarānteṣu vairāgyaṃ viṣayeṣvanu.
Yathaiva kākaviṣṭhāyāṃ vairāgyaṃ taddhi nirmalam..4..
verses.colloquial:
Brahmaadi sthaavara anteshu vairaagyam vishayeshu anu.
Yathaiva kaaka vishthaayaam vairaagyam taddhi nirmalam ..4..
verses.translation_reworded: Think of how little regard one has for a crow's droppings. To feel that same indifference toward every object of enjoyment, from the realm of Brahma down to this world (because all of them perish), is what is truly called pure Vairagya.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्यमात्मस्वरूपं हि दृश्यं तद्विपरीतगम्।
एवं यो निश्चयः सम्यग्विवेको वस्तुनः स वै।।5।।
verses.roman:
Nityamātmasvarūpaṃ hi dṛśyaṃ tadviparītagam.
Evaṃ yo niścayaḥ samyagviveko vastunaḥ sa vai..5..
verses.colloquial:
Nityam aatma svaruupam hi drishyam tad vipariita gam.
Evam yo nishchayah samyag vivekah vastunah sa vai ..5..
verses.translation_reworded: A settled conviction that Atman (the seer) alone is permanent, and that what is seen is its opposite (transient), is what is truly known as discrimination.

verses.sanskrit:
सदैव वासनात्यागः शमोऽयमिति शब्दितः।
निग्रहो बाह्यवृत्तीनां दम इत्यभिधीयते।।6।।
verses.roman:
Sadaiva vāsanātyāgaḥ śamo'yamiti śabditaḥ.
Nigraho bāhyavṛttīnāṃ dama ityabhidhīyate..6..
verses.colloquial:
Sadaiva vaasanaa tyaagah shamo' ayam iti shabditah.
Nigrahah baahya vrittiinaam dama iti abhidhiiyate ..6..
verses.translation_reworded: Giving up desires at all times is called Shama. Holding back the outward activity of the sense organs is called Dama.

verses.sanskrit:
विषयेभ्यः परावृत्तिः परमोपरतिर्हि सा।
सहनं सर्वदुःखानां तितिक्षा सा शुभा मता।।7।।
verses.roman:
Viṣayebhyaḥ parāvṛttiḥ paramoparatirhi sā.
Sahanaṃ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ titikṣā sā śubhā matā..7..
verses.colloquial:
Vishayebhyah paraavrittih parama uparatih hi saa.
Sahanam sarva duhkhaanaam titikshaa saa shubhaa mataa ..7..
verses.translation_reworded: To turn away entirely from every sense-object is the highest Uparati. To bear all sorrow and pain patiently is known as Titiksha, and it leads to happiness.

verses.sanskrit:
निगमाचार्यवाक्येषु भक्तिः श्रद्धेति विश्रुता।
चित्तैकाग्र्यं तु सल्लक्ष्ये समाधानमिति स्मृतम्।।8।।
verses.roman:
Nigamācāryavākyeṣu bhaktiḥ śraddheti viśrutā.
Cittaikāgryaṃ tu sallakṣye samādhānamiti smṛtam..8..
verses.colloquial:
Nigama aachaarya vaakyeshu bhaktih shraddhaa iti vishrutaa.
Chitta ekaagryam tu sa llakshye samaadhaanam iti smritam ..8..
verses.translation_reworded: Wholehearted faith in the words of the Vedas and of the teachers who explain them is known as Shraddha. Fixing the mind on Sat (Brahman) as its only object is regarded as Samadhana.

verses.sanskrit:
संसारबन्धनिर्मुक्तिः कथं स्यान्मे दयानिधे।
इति या सुदृढा बुद्धिर्वक्तव्या सा मुमुक्षुता।।9।।
verses.roman:
Saṃsārabandhanirmuktiḥ kathaṃ syānme dayānidhe.
Iti yā sudṛḍhā buddhirvaktavyā sā mumukṣutā..9..
verses.colloquial:
Samsaara bandha nirmuktih katham syaanme dayaanidhe.
Iti yaa sudridhaa buddhih vaktavyaa saa mumukshutaa ..9..
verses.translation_reworded: "O Lord, when and how will I be released from the bonds of this world (births and deaths)?" This burning longing is called Mumukshuta.

verses.sanskrit:
उक्तसाधनयुक्तेन विचारः पुरुषेण हि।
कर्तव्यो ज्ञानसिद्ध्यर्थमात्मनः शुभमिच्छता।।10।।
verses.roman:
Uktasādhanayuktena vicāraḥ puruṣeṇa hi.
Kartavyo jñānasiddhyarthamātmanaḥ śubhamicchatā..10..
verses.colloquial:
Uktasaadhana yuktena vichaarah purushena hi.
Kartavyah jnaana siddhyartham aatmanah shubham icchataa ..10..
verses.translation_reworded: Only someone who has these qualifications (the means to Knowledge) and who wants his own good should reflect constantly in order to gain Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
नोत्पद्यते विना ज्ञानं विचारेणान्यसाधनैः।
यथा पदार्थभानं हि प्रकाशेन विना क्वचित्।।11।।
verses.roman:
Notpadyate vinā jñānaṃ vicāreṇānyasādhanaiḥ.
Yathā padārthabhānaṃ hi prakāśena vinā kvacit..11..
verses.colloquial:
Notpadyate vinaa jnaanam vichaarena anyasaadhanaih.
Yathaa padaarthabhaanam hi prakaashena vinaa kvachit ..11..
verses.translation_reworded: Nothing but Vichara brings about Knowledge, just as no object is ever seen anywhere without the aid of light.

verses.sanskrit:
कोऽहं कथमिदं जातं को वा कर्तास्य विद्यते।
उपादानं किमस्तीह विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।12।।
verses.roman:
Ko'haṃ kathamidaṃ jātaṃ ko vā kartāsya vidyate.
Upādānaṃ kimastīha vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..12..
verses.colloquial:
Ko'ham katham idam jaatam ko vaa kartaa asya vidyate.
Upaadaanam kim asti iha vichaarah sah ayam iidrishah ..12..
verses.translation_reworded: Who am I? How did this world come about? Who made it? What is it made of? This is how Vichara (enquiry) proceeds.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहं भूतगणो देहो नाहं चाक्षगणस्तथा।
एतद्विलक्षणः कश्चिद्विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।13।।
verses.roman:
Nāhaṃ bhūtagaṇo deho nāhaṃ cākṣagaṇastathā.
Etadvilakṣaṇaḥ kaścidvicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..13..
verses.colloquial:
Naaham bhuuta gano deho naaham chaaksha ganas tathaa.
Etad vilakshanah kashchid vichaarah so'yam iidrishah ..13..
verses.translation_reworded: I am not the body, which is a combination of the five elements of matter, and I am not a collection of the senses. I am something other than these. This is how Vichara proceeds.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञानप्रभवं सर्वं ज्ञानेन प्रविलीयते।
संकल्पो विविधः कर्ता विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।14।।
verses.roman:
Ajñānaprabhavaṃ sarvaṃ jñānena pravilīyate.
Saṃkalpo vividhaḥ kartā vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..14..
verses.colloquial:
Ajnaana prabhavam sarvam jnaanena praviliiyate.
Samkalpah vividhah kartaa vichaarah so'yam iidrishah ..14..
verses.translation_reworded: Ignorance gives rise to everything, and everything dissolves when Knowledge comes. The creator must be the various thoughts (modifications of the Antahkarana). This is what Vichara finds.

verses.sanskrit:
एतयोर्यदुपादानमेकं सूक्ष्मं सदव्ययम्।
यथैव मृद्धटादीनां विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।15।।
verses.roman:
Etayoryadupādānamekaṃ sūkṣmaṃ sadavyayam.
Yathaiva mṛddhaṭādīnāṃ vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..15..
verses.colloquial:
Etayor yadupaadaanam ekam suukshmam sadavyayam.
Yathaiva mrid dhataadiinaam vichaarah so' yam iidrishah ..15..
verses.translation_reworded: Just as earth is the material of a pot and similar things, the material cause of these two (ignorance and thought) is Sat (Existence), which is one without a second, subtle (beyond the reach of the senses) and unchanging. This is how Vichara proceeds.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमेकोऽपि सूक्ष्मश्च ज्ञाता साक्षी सदव्ययः।
तदहं नात्र संदेहो विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।16।।
verses.roman:
Ahameko'pi sūkṣmaśca jñātā sākṣī sadavyayaḥ.
Tadahaṃ nātra saṃdeho vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..16..
verses.colloquial:
Ahameko'pi suukshmashcha jnaataa saakshii sadavyayah.
Tadaham naatra samdeho vichaarah so'yam iidrishah ..16..
verses.translation_reworded: Since I too am the One, the Subtle, the Knower, the Witness, the Ever-Existent and the Unchanging, I am beyond doubt "That" (Brahman). This is the enquiry.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मा विनिष्कलो ह्येको देहो बहुभिरावृतः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।17।।
verses.roman:
Ātmā viniṣkalo hyeko deho bahubhirāvṛtaḥ.
Tayoraikyaṃ prapaśyanti kimajñānamataḥ param..17..
verses.colloquial:
aatmaa vinishkalo hyeko deho bahubhir aavritah.
Tayor aikyam prapashyanti kim ajnaanam atah param ..17..
verses.translation_reworded: Atman is one and has no parts, while the body is made of many parts. Yet people look at these two and confuse them as one! What else could be called ignorance?

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मा नियामकश्चान्तर्देहो नियम्यबाह्यकः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।18।।
verses.roman:
Ātmā niyāmakaścāntardeho niyamyabāhyakaḥ.
Tayoraikyaṃ prapaśyanti kimajñānamataḥ param..18..
verses.colloquial:
aatmaa niyaamakah cha antar dehah niyamya baahyakah.
Tayor aikyam prapashyanti kim ajnaanam atah param ..18..
verses.translation_reworded: Atman is within and rules the body, while the body is outer and is ruled. Yet people confuse them as one! What else could be called ignorance?

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मा ज्ञानमयः पुण्यो देहो मांसमयोऽशुचिः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।19।।
verses.roman:
Ātmā jñānamayaḥ puṇyo deho māṃsamayo'śuciḥ.
Tayoraikyaṃ prapaśyanti kimajñānamataḥ param..19..
verses.colloquial:
aatmaa jnaanamayah punyo deho maamsamayah ashuchih.
Tayor aikyam prapashyanti kim ajnaanam atah param ..19..
verses.translation_reworded: Atman is pure consciousness and holy, while the body is pure flesh and unclean. Yet people confuse them as one! What else could be called ignorance?

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मा प्रकाशकः स्वच्छो देहस्तामस उच्यते।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।20।।
verses.roman:
Ātmā prakāśakaḥ svaccho dehastāmasa ucyate.
Tayoraikyaṃ prapaśyanti kimajñānamataḥ param..20..
verses.colloquial:
aatmaa prakaashakah svaccho dehas taamasa uchyate.
Tayor aikyam prapashyanti kim ajnaanam atah param ..20..
verses.translation_reworded: Atman is the supreme Illuminator and purity itself, while the body is said to have the nature of darkness. Yet people confuse them as one! What else could be called ignorance?

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मा नित्यो हि सद्रूपो देहोऽनित्यो ह्यसन्मयः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।21।।
verses.roman:
Ātmā nityo hi sadrūpo deho'nityo hyasanmayaḥ.
Tayoraikyaṃ prapaśyanti kimajñānamataḥ param..21..
verses.colloquial:
aatmaa nityo hi sadruupo deho 'nityo hyasanmayah.
Tayoh aikyam prapashyanti kim ajnaanam atah param ..21..
verses.translation_reworded: Atman is eternal, being Existence itself, while the body passes away, being non-existence in essence. Yet people confuse them as one! What else could be called ignorance?

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मनस्तत्प्रकाशत्वं यत्पदार्थावभासनम्।
नाग्न्यादिदीप्तिवद्दीप्तिर्भवत्यान्ध्यं यतो निशि।।22।।
verses.roman:
Ātmanastatprakāśatvaṃ yatpadārthāvabhāsanam.
Nāgnyādidīptivaddīptirbhavatyāndhyaṃ yato niśi..22..
verses.colloquial:
aatmanah tat prakaashatvam yat padaartha avabhaasanam.
Na agni aadi diipti vat diiptih bhavati andhyam yatah nishi ..22..
verses.translation_reworded: The light of Atman lies in revealing all objects. It is unlike the light of fire or anything of that kind, for even with such lights present, darkness still prevails somewhere at night.

verses.sanskrit:
देहोऽहमित्ययं मूढो मत्वा तिष्ठत्यहो जनः।
ममायमित्यपि ज्ञात्वा घटद्रष्टेव सर्वदा।।23।।
verses.roman:
Deho'hamityayaṃ mūḍho matvā tiṣṭhatyaho janaḥ.
Mamāyamityapi jñātvā ghaṭadraṣṭeva sarvadā..23..
verses.colloquial:
Deho'ham ity ayam muudho matvaa tishthaty aho janah.
Mama ayam ity api jnaatvaa ghata drashtaa iva sarvadaa ..23..
verses.translation_reworded: How strange that a person should ignorantly rest content in the idea that he is the body, when he regards it as something belonging to him, and thus separate from him, just as someone looking at a pot knows it is separate from himself!

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मैवाहं समः शान्तः सच्चिदानन्दलक्षणः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।24।।
verses.roman:
Brahmaivāhaṃ samaḥ śāntaḥ saccidānandalakṣaṇaḥ.
Nāhaṃ deho hyasadrūpo jñānamityucyate budhaiḥ..24..
verses.colloquial:
Brahma eva aham samah shaantah sat chit aananda lakshanah.
Naaham dehah hi asad ruupah jnaanam iti uchyate budhaih ..24..
verses.translation_reworded: I am truly Brahman: even-minded, at peace, by nature absolute Existence, Knowledge and Bliss. I am not the body, which is non-existence itself. The wise call this true Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्विकारो निराकारो निरवद्योऽहमव्ययः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।25।।
verses.roman:
Nirvikāro nirākāro niravadyo'hamavyayaḥ.
Nāhaṃ deho hyasadrūpo jñānamityucyate budhaiḥ..25..
verses.colloquial:
Nirvikaaro niraakaaro niravadyo'ham avyayah.
Naaham deho hyasadruupo jnaanam ity uchyate budhaih ..25..
verses.translation_reworded: I have no change and no form, and I am free from every flaw and from decay. I am not the body, which is non-existence itself. The wise call this true Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
निरामयो निराभासो निर्विकल्पोऽहमाततः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।26।।
verses.roman:
Nirāmayo nirābhāso nirvikalpo'hamātataḥ.
Nāhaṃ deho hyasadrūpo jñānamityucyate budhaiḥ..26..
verses.colloquial:
Niraamayo niraabhaaso nirvikalpo'ham aatatah.
Naaham deho hyasadruupo jnaanam iti uchyate budhaih ..26..
verses.translation_reworded: No disease can touch me. I am beyond all comprehension, free from all alternatives, and all-pervading. I am not the body, which is non-existence itself. The wise call this true Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्गुणो निष्क्रियो नित्यो नित्यमुक्तोऽहमच्युतः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।27।।
verses.roman:
Nirguṇo niṣkriyo nityo nityamukto'hamacyutaḥ.
Nāhaṃ deho hyasadrūpo jñānamityucyate budhaiḥ..27..
verses.colloquial:
Nirguno nishkriyo nityo nitya mukto'ham achyutah.
Naaham deho hyasadruupo jnaanam ity uchyate budhaih ..27..
verses.translation_reworded: I have no attributes and no activity. I am eternal, forever free and imperishable. I am not the body, which is non-existence itself. The wise call this true Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्मलो निश्चलोऽनन्तः शुद्धोऽहमजरोऽमरः।
नाहं देहो ह्यसद्रूपो ज्ञानमित्युच्यते बुधैः।।28।।
verses.roman:
Nirmalo niścalo'nantaḥ śuddho'hamajaro'maraḥ.
Nāhaṃ deho hyasadrūpo jñānamityucyate budhaiḥ..28..
verses.colloquial:
Nirmalo nishchalo 'nantah shuddho 'ham ajaro 'marah.
Naaham deho hy asadruupo jnaanam ity uchyate budhaih ..28..
verses.translation_reworded: I am free from every impurity, unmoving, unlimited, holy, undecaying and immortal. I am not the body, which is non-existence itself. The wise call this true Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वदेहं शोभनं त्यक्त्वा पुरुषाख्यं च संमतम्।
किं मूर्ख शून्यमात्मानं देहातीतं करोषि भो।।29।।
verses.roman:
Svadehaṃ śobhanaṃ tyaktvā puruṣākhyaṃ ca saṃmatam.
Kiṃ mūrkha śūnyamātmānaṃ dehātītaṃ karoṣi bho..29..
verses.colloquial:
Svadeham shobhanam tyaktvaa purushaakhyam cha sammatam.
Kim muurkha shuunyam aatmaanam dehaatiitam karoshi bho ..29..
verses.translation_reworded: You who are ignorant! The blissful, ever-existing Atman lives in your own body and is plainly different from it. It is known as Purusha, and the Shruti establishes it as identical with Brahman. Why do you insist it does not exist at all?

verses.sanskrit:
स्वात्मानं श्रृणु मूर्ख त्वं श्रुत्या युक्त्या च पूरुषम्।
देहातीतं सदाकारं सुदुर्दर्शं भवादृशाम्।।30।।
verses.roman:
Svātmānaṃ śrṛṇu mūrkha tvaṃ śrutyā yuktyā ca pūruṣam.
Dehātītaṃ sadākāraṃ sudurdarśaṃ bhavādṛśām..30..
verses.colloquial:
Svaatmaanam shrinu muurkha tvam shrutyaa yuktyaa cha puurusham.
Dehaatiitam sadaakaaram sudurdarsham bhavaadrishaam ..30..
verses.translation_reworded: You who are ignorant! With the help of Shruti and reasoning, try to know your own Self, Purusha. It is different from the body, it is not a void but the very form of existence, and it is very hard for people like you to realize.

verses.sanskrit:
अहंशब्देन विख्यात एक एव स्थितः परः।
स्थूलत्वान्नैकतां प्राप्तः कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।31।।
verses.roman:
Ahaṃśabdena vikhyāta eka eva sthitaḥ paraḥ.
Sthūlatvānnaikatāṃ prāptaḥ kathaṃ syāddehakaḥ pumān..31..
verses.colloquial:
Aham shabdena vikhyaata eka eva sthitah parah.
Sthuulatvaan naikataam praaptah katham syaad dehakah pumaan ..31..
verses.translation_reworded: The Supreme Purusha, known as "I" (ego), is one alone, while gross bodies are many. So how can this body be Purusha?

verses.sanskrit:
अहं द्रष्टृतया सिद्धो देहो दृश्यतया स्थितः।
ममायमिति निर्देशात्कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।32।।
verses.roman:
Ahaṃ draṣṭṛtayā siddho deho dṛśyatayā sthitaḥ.
Mamāyamiti nirdeśātkathaṃ syāddehakaḥ pumān..32..
verses.colloquial:
Aham drashtritayaa siddho deho drishyatayaa sthitah.
Mama ayam iti nirdeshaat katham syaat dehakah pumaan ..32..
verses.translation_reworded: The "I" (ego) is firmly established as the one who perceives, and the body as what is perceived. We can tell this because, when speaking of the body, we say, "This is mine." So how can this body be Purusha?

verses.sanskrit:
अहं विकारहीनस्तु देहो नित्यं विकारवान्।
इति प्रतीयते साक्षात्कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।33।।
verses.roman:
Ahaṃ vikārahīnastu deho nityaṃ vikāravān.
Iti pratīyate sākṣātkathaṃ syāddehakaḥ pumān..33..
verses.colloquial:
Aham vikaara hiinas tu deho nityam vikaara vaan.
Iti pratiiyate saakshaat katham syaad dehakah pumaan ..33..
verses.translation_reworded: Direct experience shows that the "I" (Atman) never changes, while the body is changing all the time. So how can this body be Purusha?

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मात्परमिति श्रुत्या तया पुरुषलक्षणम्।
विनिर्णीतं विशुद्धेन कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।34।।
verses.roman:
Yasmātparamiti śrutyā tayā puruṣalakṣaṇam.
Vinirṇītaṃ viśuddhena kathaṃ syāddehakaḥ pumān..34..
verses.colloquial:
Yasmaat param iti shrutyaa tayaa purusha lakshanam.
Vinirniitam vishuddhena katham syaat dehakah pumaan ..34..
verses.translation_reworded: Wise people have determined the true nature of Purusha from the Shruti text that begins, "There is nothing higher than He (Purusha)." So how can this body be Purusha?

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वं पुरुष एवेति सूक्ते पुरुषसंज्ञिते।
अप्युच्यते यतः श्रुत्या कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।35।।
verses.roman:
Sarvaṃ puruṣa eveti sūkte puruṣasaṃjñite.
Apyucyate yataḥ śrutyā kathaṃ syāddehakaḥ pumān..35..
verses.colloquial:
Sarvam purusha eveti suukte purusha samjnite.
Api uchyate yatah shrutyaa katham syaat dehakah pumaan ..35..
verses.translation_reworded: The Shruti also declares in the Purusha Sukta, "All this is indeed the Purusha." So how can this body be Purusha?

verses.sanskrit:
असङ्गः पुरुषः प्रोक्तो बृहदारण्यकेऽपि च।
अनन्तमलसंसृष्टः कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।36।।
verses.roman:
Asaṅgaḥ puruṣaḥ prokto bṛhadāraṇyake'pi ca.
Anantamalasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ kathaṃ syāddehakaḥ pumān..36..
verses.colloquial:
Asangah purushah prokto brihad aaranyake'pi cha.
Ananta mala samsrishtah katham syaad dehakah pumaan ..36..
verses.translation_reworded: In the same way, the Brihadaranyaka says, "The Purusha is entirely unattached." How can this body, in which countless impurities reside, be the Purusha?

verses.sanskrit:
तत्रैव च समाख्यातः स्वयंज्योतिर्हि पूरुषः।
जडः परप्रकाश्योऽयं कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।37।।
verses.roman:
Tatraiva ca samākhyātaḥ svayaṃjyotirhi pūruṣaḥ.
Jaḍaḥ paraprakāśyo'yaṃ kathaṃ syāddehakaḥ pumān..37..
verses.colloquial:
Tatraiva cha samaakhyaatah svayam jyotih hi puurushah.
Jadah para prakaashyah ayam katham syaat dehakah pumaan ..37..
verses.translation_reworded: The same text also plainly states, "The Purusha is self-illumined." So how can the body, which is inert (insentient) and lit by something outside itself, be the Purusha?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रोक्तोऽपि कर्मकाण्डेन ह्यात्मा देहाद्विलक्षणः।
नित्यश्च तत्फलं भुङ्क्ते देहपातादनन्तरम्।।38।।
verses.roman:
Prokto'pi karmakāṇḍena hyātmā dehādvilakṣaṇaḥ.
Nityaśca tatphalaṃ bhuṅkte dehapātādanantaram..38..
verses.colloquial:
Prokto'pi karma kaandena hyaatmaa dehaad vilakshanah.
Nityashcha tat phalam bhunkte deha paataad anantaram ..38..
verses.translation_reworded: The Karma-kanda too declares that the Atman is permanent and distinct from the body, because it continues after the body has fallen and reaps the results of actions done in this life.

verses.sanskrit:
लिङ्गं चानेकसंयुक्तं चलं दृश्यं विकारि च।
अव्यापकमसद्रूपं तत्कथं स्यात्पुमानयम्।।39।।
verses.roman:
Liṅgaṃ cānekasaṃyuktaṃ calaṃ dṛśyaṃ vikāri ca.
Avyāpakamasadrūpaṃ tatkathaṃ syātpumānayam..39..
verses.colloquial:
Lingam cha aneka samyuktam chalam drishyam vikaari cha.
Avyaapakam asadruupam tat katham syaat pumaan ayam ..39..
verses.translation_reworded: Even the subtle body is made of many parts and is unstable. It is also perceived as an object, and it is changeable, limited and non-existent by nature. So how can this be the Purusha?

verses.sanskrit:
एवं देहद्वयादन्य आत्मा पुरुष ईश्वरः।
सर्वात्मा सर्वरूपश्च सर्वातीतोऽहमव्ययः।।40।।
verses.roman:
Evaṃ dehadvayādanya ātmā puruṣa īśvaraḥ.
Sarvātmā sarvarūpaśca sarvātīto'hamavyayaḥ..40..
verses.colloquial:
Evam deha dvayaad anya aatmaa purusha iishvarah.
Sarvaatmaa sarva ruupash cha sarva atiitah aham avyayah ..40..
verses.translation_reworded: So the unchanging Atman, the ground of the ego, is different from these two bodies. It is the Purusha, the Ishwara (the Lord of all), the Self of all. It is present in every form and still goes beyond them all.

verses.sanskrit:
इत्यात्मदेहभानेन प्रपञ्चस्यैव सत्यता।
यथोक्ता तर्कशास्त्रेण ततः किं पुरुषार्थता।।41।।
verses.roman:
Ityātmadehabhānena prapañcasyaiva satyatā.
Yathoktā tarkaśāstreṇa tataḥ kiṃ puruṣārthatā..41..
verses.colloquial:
Ityaatmadeha bhaanena prapanchasyaiva satyataa.
Yathoktaa tarkashaastrena tatah kim purushaarthataa ..41..
verses.translation_reworded: By stating the difference between the Atman and the body in this way, the reality of the phenomenal world has been affirmed indirectly, in the manner of the Tarkashastra. But what human goal does that achieve?

verses.sanskrit:
इत्यात्मदेहभेदेन देहात्मत्वं निवारितम्।
इदानीं देहभेदस्य ह्यसत्त्वं स्फुटमुच्यते।।42।।
verses.roman:
Ityātmadehabhedena dehātmatvaṃ nivāritam.
Idānīṃ dehabhedasya hyasattvaṃ sphuṭamucyate..42..
verses.colloquial:
Ityaatmadeha bhedena dehaatmatvam nivaaritam.
Idaaniim deha bhedasya hyasattvam sphutam uchyate ..42..
verses.translation_reworded: The view that the body is the Atman has thus been refuted by stating the difference between the two. Now it is plainly stated that this difference is itself unreal.

verses.sanskrit:
चैतन्यस्यैकरूपत्वाद्भेदो युक्तो न कर्हिचित्।
जीवत्वं च मृषा ज्ञेयं रज्ज्वां सर्पग्रहो यथा।।43।।
verses.roman:
Caitanyasyaikarūpatvādbhedo yukto na karhicit.
Jīvatvaṃ ca mṛṣā jñeyaṃ rajjvāṃ sarpagraho yathā..43..
verses.colloquial:
Chaitanyasya ekaruupatvaad bhedo yukto na karhichit.
Jiivatvam cha mrishaa jneyam rajjvaam sarpagraho yathaa ..43..
verses.translation_reworded: Consciousness is always one and the same, so it can never be admitted to have divisions. Even the individuality of the Jiva must be understood as false, like mistaking a rope for a snake.

verses.sanskrit:
रज्ज्वज्ञानात्क्षणेनैव यद्वद्रज्जुर्हि सर्पिणी।
भाति तद्वच्चितिः साक्षाद्विश्वाकारेण केवला।।44।।
verses.roman:
Rajjvajñānātkṣaṇenaiva yadvadrajjurhi sarpiṇī.
Bhāti tadvaccitiḥ sākṣādviśvākāreṇa kevalā..44..
verses.colloquial:
Rajjvajnaanaat kshanenaiva yadvad rajjur hi sarpinii.
Bhaati tadvac chitih saakshaad vishvaakaarena kevalaa ..44..
verses.translation_reworded: When the true nature of a rope is not known, that very rope appears in a moment to be a snake. In the same way, pure Consciousness appears as the phenomenal universe without undergoing any change.

verses.sanskrit:
उपादानं प्रपञ्चस्य ब्रह्मणोऽन्यन्न विद्यते।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रपञ्चोऽयं ब्रह्मैवास्ति न चेतरत्।।45।।
verses.roman:
Upādānaṃ prapañcasya brahmaṇo'nyanna vidyate.
Tasmātsarvaprapañco'yaṃ brahmaivāsti na cetarat..45..
verses.colloquial:
Upaadaanam prapanchasya brahmano'nyanna vidyate.
Tasmaat sarva prapancho'yam brahmaiva asti na chetarat ..45..
verses.translation_reworded: This phenomenal universe has no material cause other than Brahman. So the whole universe is only Brahman and nothing else.

verses.sanskrit:
व्याप्यव्यापकता मिथ्या सर्वमात्मेति शासनात्।
इति ज्ञाते परे तत्त्वे भेदस्यावसरः कुतः।।46।।
verses.roman:
Vyāpyavyāpakatā mithyā sarvamātmeti śāsanāt.
Iti jñāte pare tattve bhedasyāvasaraḥ kutaḥ..46..
verses.colloquial:
Vyaapya vyaapakataa mithyaa sarvam aatmeti shaasanaat.
Iti jnaate pare tattve bhedasya avasarah kutah ..46..
verses.translation_reworded: From such statements of the Shruti as "All this is Atman," it follows that the notion of what pervades and what is pervaded is an illusion. Once this supreme truth is realized, what room is left for any distinction between cause and effect?

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्या निवारितं नूनं नानात्वं स्वमुखेन हि।
कथं भासो भवेदन्यः स्थिते चाद्वयकारणे।।47।।
verses.roman:
Śrutyā nivāritaṃ nūnaṃ nānātvaṃ svamukhena hi.
Kathaṃ bhāso bhavedanyaḥ sthite cādvayakāraṇe..47..
verses.colloquial:
shrutyaa nivaaritam nuunam naanaatvam svamukhena hi.
Katham bhaasah bhavet anyah sthite cha advaya kaarane ..47..
verses.translation_reworded: The Shruti has directly denied that there is any manifoldness in Brahman. Since the non-dual cause is an established fact, how could the phenomenal universe be different from It?

verses.sanskrit:
दोषोऽपि विहितः श्रुत्या मृत्योर्मृत्युं स गच्छति।
इह पश्यति नानात्वं मायया वञ्चितो नरः।।48।।
verses.roman:
Doṣo'pi vihitaḥ śrutyā mṛtyormṛtyuṃ sa gacchati.
Iha paśyati nānātvaṃ māyayā vañcito naraḥ..48..
verses.colloquial:
Dosho'pi vihitah shrutyaa mrityor mrityum sa gacchati.
Iha pashyati naanaatvam maayayaa vanchito narah ..48..
verses.translation_reworded: The Shruti has also condemned the belief in variety, saying that the person deceived by Maya who "sees variety in this (Brahman), goes from death to death."

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मणः सर्वभूतानि जायन्ते परमात्मनः।
तस्मादेतानि ब्रह्मैव भवन्तीत्यवधारयेत्।।49।।
verses.roman:
Brahmaṇaḥ sarvabhūtāni jāyante paramātmanaḥ.
Tasmādetāni brahmaiva bhavantītyavadhārayet..49..
verses.colloquial:
Brahmanah sarva bhuutaani jaayante paramaatmanah.
Tasmaad etaani brahmaiva bhavanti iti avadhaarayet ..49..
verses.translation_reworded: Since all beings are born of Brahman, the supreme Atman, they must be understood to be Brahman itself.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मैव सर्वनामानि रूपाणि विविधानि च।
कर्माण्यपि समग्राणि बिभर्तीति श्रुतिर्जगौ।।50।।
verses.roman:
Brahmaiva sarvanāmāni rūpāṇi vividhāni ca.
Karmāṇyapi samagrāṇi bibhartīti śrutirjagau..50..
verses.colloquial:
Brahmaiva sarva naamaani ruupaani vividhaani cha.
Karmaani api samagraani bibharti iti shrutih jagau ..50..
verses.translation_reworded: The Shruti has plainly declared that Brahman alone is the underlying ground of all the varied names, forms and actions.

verses.sanskrit:
सुवर्णाज्जायमानस्य सुवर्णत्वं च शाश्वतम्।
ब्रह्मणो जायमानस्य ब्रह्मत्वं च तथा भवेत्।।51।।
verses.roman:
Suvarṇājjāyamānasya suvarṇatvaṃ ca śāśvatam.
Brahmaṇo jāyamānasya brahmatvaṃ ca tathā bhavet..51..
verses.colloquial:
Suvarnaat jaayamaanasya suvarnatvam cha shaashvatam.
Brahmanah jaayamaanasya brahmatvam cha tathaa bhavet ..51..
verses.translation_reworded: Just as whatever is made of gold always has the nature of gold, whatever is born of Brahman always has the nature of Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वल्पमप्यन्तरं कृत्वा जीवात्मपरमात्मनोः।
योऽवतिष्ठति मूढात्मा भयं तस्याभिभाषितम्।।52।।
verses.roman:
Svalpamapyantaraṃ kṛtvā jīvātmaparamātmanoḥ.
Yo'vatiṣṭhati mūḍhātmā bhayaṃ tasyābhibhāṣitam..52..
verses.colloquial:
Svalpam api antaram kritvaa jiivaatma paramaatmanoh.
Yo'vatishthati muudhaatmaa bhayam tasya abhibhaashitam ..52..
verses.translation_reworded: Fear is said to belong to the ignorant person who settles into making even the smallest distinction between the Jivatman and the Paramatman.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्राज्ञानाद्भवेद्द्वैतमितरस्तत्र पश्यति।
आत्मत्वेन यदा सर्वं नेतरस्तत्र चाण्वपि।।53।।
verses.roman:
Yatrājñānādbhaveddvaitamitarastatra paśyati.
Ātmatvena yadā sarvaṃ netarastatra cāṇvapi..53..
verses.colloquial:
Yatra ajnaanaad bhavet dvaitam itaras tatra pashyati.
aatmatvena yadaa sarvam na itaras tatra cha anu api ..53..
verses.translation_reworded: When duality appears because of ignorance, one person sees another. But when everything has become one with the Atman, nobody perceives another, not even slightly.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्मिन्सर्वाणि भूतानि ह्यात्मत्वेन विजानतः।
न वै तस्य भवेन्मोहो न च शोकोऽद्वितीयतः।।54।।
verses.roman:
Yasminsarvāṇi bhūtāni hyātmatvena vijānataḥ.
Na vai tasya bhavenmoho na ca śoko'dvitīyataḥ..54..
verses.colloquial:
Yasmin sarvaani bhuutaani hyaatmatvena vijaanatah.
Na vai tasya bhavet moho na cha shokah advitiiyatah ..54..
verses.translation_reworded: In the state where one realizes everything as one with the Atman, neither delusion nor sorrow arises, because duality is absent.

verses.sanskrit:
अयमात्मा हि ब्रह्मैव सर्वात्मकतया स्थितः।
इति निर्धारितं श्रुत्या बृहदारण्यसंस्थया।।55।।
verses.roman:
Ayamātmā hi brahmaiva sarvātmakatayā sthitaḥ.
Iti nirdhāritaṃ śrutyā bṛhadāraṇyasaṃsthayā..55..
verses.colloquial:
Ayam aatmaa hi brahmaiva sarva aatmakatayaa sthitah.
Iti nirdhaaritam shrutyaa brihad aaranya samsthayaa ..55..
verses.translation_reworded: The Shruti, in the form of the Brihadaranyaka, has declared that this Atman, the Self of all, is truly Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुभूतोऽप्ययं लोको व्यवहारक्षमोऽपि सन्।
असद्रूपो यथा स्वप्न उत्तरक्षणबाधतः।।56।।
verses.roman:
Anubhūto'pyayaṃ loko vyavahārakṣamo'pi san.
Asadrūpo yathā svapna uttarakṣaṇabādhataḥ..56..
verses.colloquial:
Anubhuuto'pyayam loko vyavahaara kshamo'pi san.
Asadruupo yathaa svapna uttara kshana baadhatah ..56..
verses.translation_reworded: We experience this world daily and it serves every practical purpose, yet, like the world of a dream, it is of the nature of non-existence, because it is contradicted the very next moment.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्नो जागरणेऽलीकः स्वप्नेऽपि न हि जागरः।
द्वयमेव लये नास्ति लयोऽपि ह्युभयोर्न च।।57।।
verses.roman:
Svapno jāgaraṇe'līkaḥ svapne'pi na hi jāgaraḥ.
Dvayameva laye nāsti layo'pi hyubhayorna ca..57..
verses.colloquial:
Svapno jaagarane aliikah svapne api na hi jaagarah.
Dvayam eva laye naasti layah api hi ubhayoh na cha ..57..
verses.translation_reworded: Dream experience is unreal once we are awake, and waking experience is absent in a dream. Neither exists in deep sleep, and deep sleep in turn is not experienced in either of the other two.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रयमेवं भवेन्मिथ्या गुणत्रयविनिर्मितम्।
अस्य द्रष्टा गुणातीतो नित्यो ह्येकश्चिदात्मकः।।58।।
verses.roman:
Trayamevaṃ bhavenmithyā guṇatrayavinirmitam.
Asya draṣṭā guṇātīto nityo hyekaścidātmakaḥ..58..
verses.colloquial:
Trayam evam bhavet mithyaa guna traya vinirmitam.
Asya drashtaa gunaatiitah nityah hi ekah chit aatmakah ..58..
verses.translation_reworded: So all three states are unreal, being products of the three Gunas. But their witness, the reality behind them, is beyond all Gunas, eternal, one, and Consciousness itself.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्वन्मृदि घटभ्रान्तिं शुक्तौ वा रजतस्थितिम्।
तद्वद्ब्रह्मणि जीवत्वं भ्रान्त्या पश्यति न स्वतः।।59।।
verses.roman:
Yadvanmṛdi ghaṭabhrāntiṃ śuktau vā rajatasthitim.
Tadvadbrahmaṇi jīvatvaṃ bhrāntyā paśyati na svataḥ..59..
verses.colloquial:
Yadvan mridi ghata bhraantim shuktau vaa rajata sthitim.
Tadvat brahmani jiivatvam bhraantyaa pashyati na svatah ..59..
verses.translation_reworded: Once the illusion has gone, a person is no longer fooled into seeing a jar in earth or silver in nacre. In the same way, one no longer sees a Jiva in Brahman when Brahman has been realized as one's own self.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा मृदि घटो नाम कनके कुण्डलाभिधा।
शुक्तौ हि रजतख्यातिर्जीवशब्दस्तथा परे।।60।।
verses.roman:
Yathā mṛdi ghaṭo nāma kanake kuṇḍalābhidhā.
Śuktau hi rajatakhyātirjīvaśabdastathā pare..60..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaa mridi ghato naama kanake kundala abhidhaa.
shuktau hi rajata khyaatir jiiva shabdas tathaa pare ..60..
verses.translation_reworded: Just as earth is spoken of as a jar, gold as an earring, and nacre as silver, Brahman is spoken of as Jiva.

verses.sanskrit:
यथैव व्योम्नि नीलत्वं यथा नीरं मरुस्थले।
पुरुषत्वं यथा स्थाणौ तद्वद्विश्वं चिदात्मनि।।61।।
verses.roman:
Yathaiva vyomni nīlatvaṃ yathā nīraṃ marusthale.
Puruṣatvaṃ yathā sthāṇau tadvadviśvaṃ cidātmani..61..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaiva vyomni niilatvam yathaa niiram marusthale.
Purushatvam yathaa sthaanau tadvat vishvam chit aatmani ..61..
verses.translation_reworded: The universe in Atman is like blueness in the sky, water in a mirage, or a human figure seen in a post: (all of them merely illusory).

verses.sanskrit:
यथैव शून्ये वेतालो गन्धर्वाणां पुरं यथा।
यथाकाशे द्विचन्द्रत्वं तद्वत्सत्ये जगत्स्थितिः।।62।।
verses.roman:
Yathaiva śūnye vetālo gandharvāṇāṃ puraṃ yathā.
Yathākāśe dvicandratvaṃ tadvatsatye jagatsthitiḥ..62..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaiva shuunye vetaalo gandharvaanaam puram yathaa.
Yathaakaashe dvichandra tvam tadvat satye jagat sthitih ..62..
verses.translation_reworded: The universe appears in Brahman the way a ghost appears in an empty place, a castle in the air, or a second moon in the sky: (the appearance is illusory).

verses.sanskrit:
यथा तरङ्गकल्लोलैर्जलमेव स्फुरत्यलम्।
पात्ररूपेण ताम्रं हि ब्रह्माण्डौघैस्तथात्मता।।63।।
verses.roman:
Yathā taraṅgakallolairjalameva sphuratyalam.
Pātrarūpeṇa tāmraṃ hi brahmāṇḍaughaistathātmatā..63..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaa taranga kallolair jalam eva sphuratyalam.
Paatra ruupena taamram hi brahmaandaughais tathaa aatmataa ..63..
verses.translation_reworded: Ripples and waves are only water appearing in those shapes, and a vessel is only copper in that form. In the same way, it is Atman that appears as the entire universe.

verses.sanskrit:
घटनाम्ना यथा पृथ्वी पटनाम्ना हि तन्तवः।
जगन्नाम्ना चिदाभाति ज्ञेयं तत्तदभावतः।।64।।
verses.roman:
Ghaṭanāmnā yathā pṛthvī paṭanāmnā hi tantavaḥ.
Jagannāmnā cidābhāti jñeyaṃ tattadabhāvataḥ..64..
verses.colloquial:
Ghata naamnaa yathaa prithvii pata naamnaa hi tantavah.
Jagat naamnaa chit aabhaati jneyam tat tad abhaavatah ..64..
verses.translation_reworded: Earth is what appears under the name "jar," and threads are what appear under the name "cloth." Likewise, Atman is what appears under the name "universe." This Atman is to be known by setting the names aside.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वोऽपि व्यवहारस्तु ब्रह्मणा क्रियते जनैः।
अज्ञानान्न विजानन्ति मृदेव हि घटादिकम्।।65।।
verses.roman:
Sarvo'pi vyavahārastu brahmaṇā kriyate janaiḥ.
Ajñānānna vijānanti mṛdeva hi ghaṭādikam..65..
verses.colloquial:
Sarvo'pi vyavahaaras tu brahmanaa kriyate janaih.
Ajnaanaanna vijaananti mrid eva hi ghataadikam ..65..
verses.translation_reworded: Everything people do, they do in and through Brahman, (but ignorance keeps them unaware of it), just as ignorance keeps people from seeing that jars and other earthenware are nothing but earth.

verses.sanskrit:
कार्यकारणता नित्यमास्ते घटमृदोर्यथा।
तथैव श्रुतियुक्तिभ्यां प्रपञ्चब्रह्मणोरिह।।66।।
verses.roman:
Kāryakāraṇatā nityamāste ghaṭamṛdoryathā.
Tathaiva śrutiyuktibhyāṃ prapañcabrahmaṇoriha..66..
verses.colloquial:
Kaarya kaaranataa nityam aaste ghata mridoh yathaa.
Tathaiva shruti yuktibhyaam prapancha brahmanah iha ..66..
verses.translation_reworded: The relation of cause and effect that always holds between earth and a jar also holds between Brahman and the phenomenal world. Scriptural texts and reasoning have established this here.

verses.sanskrit:
गृह्यमाणे घटे यद्वन्मृत्तिका भाति वै बलात्।
वीक्ष्यमाणे प्रपञ्चेऽपि ब्रह्मैवाभाति भासुरम्।।67।।
verses.roman:
Gṛhyamāṇe ghaṭe yadvanmṛttikā bhāti vai balāt.
Vīkṣyamāṇe prapañce'pi brahmaivābhāti bhāsuram..67..
verses.colloquial:
Grihyamaane ghate yadvan mrittikaa bhaati vai balaat.
Viikshyamaane prapanche'pi brahma eva abhaati bhaasuram ..67..
verses.translation_reworded: When we think of a jar, (the awareness of) earth presses itself on the mind. In the same way, when we reflect on the phenomenal world, (the idea of) ever-shining Brahman flashes upon us.

verses.sanskrit:
सदैवात्मा विशुद्धोऽपि ह्यशुद्धो भाति वै सदा।
यथैव द्विविधा रज्जुर्ज्ञानिनोऽज्ञानिनोऽनिशम्।।68।।
verses.roman:
Sadaivātmā viśuddho'pi hyaśuddho bhāti vai sadā.
Yathaiva dvividhā rajjurjñānino'jñānino'niśam..68..
verses.colloquial:
Sadaiva aatmaa vishuddho'pi hyashuddho bhaati vai sadaa.
Yathaiva dvividhaa rajjuh jnaanino'jnaanino'nisham ..68..
verses.translation_reworded: Atman is always pure (to the wise), yet it always seems impure (to the ignorant), just as one rope always looks two different ways to the person who knows and the person who does not.

verses.sanskrit:
यथैव मृन्मयः कुम्भस्तद्वद्देहोऽपि चिन्मयः।
आत्मानात्मविभागोऽयं मुधैव क्रियते बुधैः।।69।।
verses.roman:
Yathaiva mṛnmayaḥ kumbhastadvaddeho'pi cinmayaḥ.
Ātmānātmavibhāgo'yaṃ mudhaiva kriyate budhaiḥ..69..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaiva mrinmayah kumbhas tadvad deho'pi chinmayah.
aatmaa anaatma vibhaagah ayam mudhaiva kriyate budhaih ..69..
verses.translation_reworded: A jar is earth through and through, and the body is consciousness through and through. So the ignorant gain nothing by dividing things into the Self and the non-Self.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्पत्वेन यथा रज्जू रजतत्वेन शुक्तिका।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।70।।
verses.roman:
Sarpatvena yathā rajjū rajatatvena śuktikā.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..70..
verses.colloquial:
Sarpatvena yathaa rajjuu rajatatvena shuktikaa.
Vinirniitaa vimuudhena dehatvena tathaa aatmataa ..70..
verses.translation_reworded: An ignorant person takes the Atman to be the body, just as a rope is imagined to be a snake and a piece of nacre is imagined to be silver.

verses.sanskrit:
घटत्वेन यथा पृथ्वी पटत्वेनैव तन्तवः।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।71।।
verses.roman:
Ghaṭatvena yathā pṛthvī paṭatvenaiva tantavaḥ.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..71..
verses.colloquial:
Ghatatvena yathaa prithvii patatvenaiva tantavah.
Vinirniitaa vimuudhena dehatvena tathaa aatmataa ..71..
verses.translation_reworded: People think of earth as a jar (shaped from it) and of threads as a cloth; the Atman is treated likewise, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
कनकं कुण्डलत्वेन तरङ्गत्वेन वै जलम्।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।72।।
verses.roman:
Kanakaṃ kuṇḍalatvena taraṅgatvena vai jalam.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..72..
verses.colloquial:
Kanakam kundala tvena taranga tvena vai jalam.
Vinirniitaa vimuudhena deha tvena tathaa aatmataa ..72..
verses.translation_reworded: As gold is thought of as an earring and water as waves, so is the Atman, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
पुरुषत्वेन वै स्थाणुर्जलत्वेन मरीचिका।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।73।।
verses.roman:
Puruṣatvena vai sthāṇurjalatvena marīcikā.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..73..
verses.colloquial:
Purushatvena vai sthaanur jalatvena mariichikaa.
Vinirniitaa vimuudhena dehatvena tathaa aatmataa ..73..
verses.translation_reworded: As a tree stump is mistaken for a human figure and a mirage for water, so is the Atman, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
गृहत्वेनैव काष्ठानि खङ्गत्वेनैव लोहता।
विनिर्णीता विमूढेन देहत्वेन तथात्मता।।74।।
verses.roman:
Gṛhatvenaiva kāṣṭhāni khaṅgatvenaiva lohatā.
Vinirṇītā vimūḍhena dehatvena tathātmatā..74..
verses.colloquial:
Grihatvenaiva kaashthaani khangatvenaiva lohataa.
Vinirniitaa vimuudhena dehatvena tathaa aatmataa ..74..
verses.translation_reworded: As an assembly of woodwork is thought of as a house and iron as a sword, so is the Atman, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा वृक्षविपर्यासो जलाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।75।।
verses.roman:
Yathā vṛkṣaviparyāso jalādbhavati kasyacit.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..75..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaa vriksha viparyaaso jalaad bhavati kasyachit.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..75..
verses.translation_reworded: As one sees an illusory tree because of water, so a person sees Atman as the body because of ignorance.

verses.sanskrit:
पोतेन गच्छतः पुंसः सर्वं भातीव चञ्चलम्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।76।।
verses.roman:
Potena gacchataḥ puṃsaḥ sarvaṃ bhātīva cañcalam.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..76..
verses.colloquial:
Potena gacchatah pumsah sarvam bhaatiiva chanchalam.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..76..
verses.translation_reworded: As everything seems to be moving to someone travelling in a boat, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
पीतत्वं हि यथा शुभ्रे दोषाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।77।।
verses.roman:
Pītatvaṃ hi yathā śubhre doṣādbhavati kasyacit.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..77..
verses.colloquial:
Piitatvam hi yathaa shubhre doshaad bhavati kasyachit.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..77..
verses.translation_reworded: As white things look yellow to someone with a defect (jaundice), so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
चक्षुर्भ्यां भ्रमशीलाभ्यां सर्वं भाति भ्रमात्मकम्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।78।।
verses.roman:
Cakṣurbhyāṃ bhramaśīlābhyāṃ sarvaṃ bhāti bhramātmakam.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..78..
verses.colloquial:
Chakshurbhyaam bhramashiilaabhyaam sarvam bhaati bhrama aatmakam.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..78..
verses.translation_reworded: As everything looks defective to someone whose eyes are defective, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
अलातं भ्रमणेनैव वर्तुलं भाति सूर्यवत्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।79।।
verses.roman:
Alātaṃ bhramaṇenaiva vartulaṃ bhāti sūryavat.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..79..
verses.colloquial:
Alaatam bhramanenaiva vartulam bhaati suuryavat.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..79..
verses.translation_reworded: As a firebrand, simply by being whirled around, looks circular like the sun, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
महत्त्वे सर्ववस्तूनामणुत्वं ह्यतिदूरतः।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।80।।
verses.roman:
Mahattve sarvavastūnāmaṇutvaṃ hyatidūrataḥ.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..80..
verses.colloquial:
Mahattve sarva vastuunaam anutvam hyatiduuratah.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..80..
verses.translation_reworded: As things that are truly large look tiny from a great distance, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
सूक्ष्मत्वे सर्ववस्तूनां स्थूलत्वं चोपनेत्रतः।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।81।।
verses.roman:
Sūkṣmatve sarvavastūnāṃ sthūlatvaṃ copanetrataḥ.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..81..
verses.colloquial:
Suukshmatve sarva vastuunaam sthuulatvam cha upanetratah.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..81..
verses.translation_reworded: As very small objects look large through lenses, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
काचभूमौ जलत्वं वा जलभूमौ हि काचता।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।82।।
verses.roman:
Kācabhūmau jalatvaṃ vā jalabhūmau hi kācatā.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..82..
verses.colloquial:
Kaacha bhuumau jalatvam vaa jala bhuumau hi kaachataa.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..82..
verses.translation_reworded: As a glass surface is mistaken for water, or water for glass, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्वदग्नौ मणित्वं हि मणौ वा वह्निता पुमान्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।83।।
verses.roman:
Yadvadagnau maṇitvaṃ hi maṇau vā vahnitā pumān.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..83..
verses.colloquial:
Yadvad agnau manitvam hi manau vaa vahnitaa pumaan.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..83..
verses.translation_reworded: As someone imagines a jewel in fire, or fire in a jewel, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
अभ्रेषु सत्सु धावत्सु धावन्निव यथा शशी।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।84।।
verses.roman:
Abhreṣu satsu dhāvatsu dhāvanniva yathā śaśī.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..84..
verses.colloquial:
Abhreshu satsu dhaavatsu dhaavanniva yathaa shashii.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..84..
verses.translation_reworded: As the moon seems to move when the clouds are moving, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
यथैव दिग्विपर्यासो मोहाद्भवति कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।85।।
verses.roman:
Yathaiva digviparyāso mohādbhavati kasyacit.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..85..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaiva dig viparyaaso mohaad bhavati kasyachit.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..85..
verses.translation_reworded: As a confused person loses all sense of the different directions of the compass, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा शशी जले भाति चञ्चलत्वेन कस्यचित्।
तद्वदात्मनि देहत्वं पश्यत्यज्ञानयोगतः।।86।।
verses.roman:
Yathā śaśī jale bhāti cañcalatvena kasyacit.
Tadvadātmani dehatvaṃ paśyatyajñānayogataḥ..86..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaa shashii jale bhaati chanchalatvena kasyachit.
Tadvat aatmani dehatvam pashyati ajnaana yogatah ..86..
verses.translation_reworded: As the moon (reflected) in water seems unsteady, so does one, etc.

verses.sanskrit:
एवमात्मनि नज्ञाते देहाध्यासो हि जायते।
स एवात्मा परिज्ञातो लीयते च परात्मनि।।87।।
verses.roman:
Evamātmani najñāte dehādhyāso hi jāyate.
Sa evātmā parijñāto līyate ca parātmani..87..
verses.colloquial:
Evam aatmani na jnaate deha adhyaaso hi jaayate.
Sa eva aatmaa parijnaato liiyate cha paraatmani ..87..
verses.translation_reworded: In this way, ignorance gives rise in Atman to the delusion of the body, and through Self-realization that delusion vanishes in the supreme Atman.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वमात्मतया ज्ञातं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम्।
अभावात्सर्वभावानां देहानां चात्मता कुतः।।88।।
verses.roman:
Sarvamātmatayā jñātaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam.
Abhāvātsarvabhāvānāṃ dehānāṃ cātmatā kutaḥ..88..
verses.colloquial:
Sarvam aatmatayaa jnaatam jagat sthaavara jangamam.
Abhaavaat sarva bhaavaanaam dehaanaam cha aatmataa kutah ..88..
verses.translation_reworded: Once the whole universe, moving and unmoving, is known to be Atman, and the existence of anything else is thereby denied, what room is left for saying that the body is Atman?

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानं सततं जानन्कालं नय महामते।
प्रारब्धमखिलं भुञ्जन्नोद्वेगं कर्तुमर्हसि।।89।।
verses.roman:
Ātmānaṃ satataṃ jānankālaṃ naya mahāmate.
Prārabdhamakhilaṃ bhuñjannodvegaṃ kartumarhasi..89..
verses.colloquial:
aatmaanam satatam jaanankaalam naya mahaamate.
Praarabdham akhilam bhunjan nodvegam kartum arhasi ..89..
verses.translation_reworded: O enlightened one, spend your time always reflecting on Atman while you undergo all the results of Prarabdha. It does not suit you to feel distressed.

verses.sanskrit:
उत्पन्नेऽप्यात्मविज्ञाने प्रारब्धं नैव मुञ्चति।
इति यच्छ्रूयते शास्त्रात्तन्निराक्रियतेऽधुना।।90।।
verses.roman:
Utpanne'pyātmavijñāne prārabdhaṃ naiva muñcati.
Iti yacchrūyate śāstrāttannirākriyate'dhunā..90..
verses.colloquial:
Utpanne'pi aatmavijnaane praarabdham naiva munchati.
Iti yat shruuyate shaastraat tat niraakriyate adhunaa ..90..
verses.translation_reworded: Scripture is heard to teach that Prarabdha keeps its grip on a person even after knowledge of Atman has arisen. That theory is now refuted.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्त्वज्ञानोदयादूर्ध्वं प्रारब्धं नैव विद्यते।
देहादीनामसत्यत्वाद्यथा स्वप्नः प्रबोधतः।।91।।
verses.roman:
Tattvajñānodayādūrdhvaṃ prārabdhaṃ naiva vidyate.
Dehādīnāmasatyatvādyathā svapnaḥ prabodhataḥ..91..
verses.colloquial:
Tattva jnaana udayaad uurdhvam praarabdham naiva vidyate.
Deha aadiinaam asatyatvaad yathaa svapnah prabodhatah ..91..
verses.translation_reworded: Once knowledge of Reality has arisen, Prarabdha truly ceases to exist, since the body and the like are no longer real, just as a dream does not exist after waking.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्म जन्मान्तरकृतं प्रारब्धमिति कीर्तितम्।
तत्तु जन्मान्तराभावात्पुंसो नैवास्ति कर्हिचित्।।92।।
verses.roman:
Karma janmāntarakṛtaṃ prārabdhamiti kīrtitam.
Tattu janmāntarābhāvātpuṃso naivāsti karhicit..92..
verses.colloquial:
Karma janmaantara kritam praarabdha miti kiirtitam.
Tattu janmaantara abhaavaat pumso naiva asti karhichit ..92..
verses.translation_reworded: Karma done in a previous life is called Prarabdha (and produces the present life). But such Karma cannot serve as Prarabdha (for a person of knowledge), since he has no further birth (being free from ego).

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्नदेहो यथाध्यस्तस्तथैवायं हि देहकः।।
अध्यस्तस्य कुतो जन्म जन्माभावे स्थितिः कुतः।।93।।
verses.roman:
Svapnadeho yathādhyastastathaivāyaṃ hi dehakaḥ..
Adhyastasya kuto janma janmābhāve sthitiḥ kutaḥ..93..
verses.colloquial:
Svapna deho yathaa adhyastah tathaiva ayam hi dehakah..
Adhyastasya kuto janma janma abhaave sthitih kutah ..93..
verses.translation_reworded: This body is superimposed (and so illusory), just as the body in a dream is. How could something superimposed be born? And if (the body) has no birth, what room is there for that (Prarabdha) at all?

verses.sanskrit:
उपादानं प्रपञ्चस्य मृद्भाण्डस्येव कथ्यते।
अज्ञानं चैव वेदान्तैस्तस्मिन्नष्टे क्व विश्वता।।94।।
verses.roman:
Upādānaṃ prapañcasya mṛdbhāṇḍasyeva kathyate.
Ajñānaṃ caiva vedāntaistasminnaṣṭe kva viśvatā..94..
verses.colloquial:
Upaadaanam prapanchasya mridbhaandasya eva kathyate.
Ajnaanam cha eva vedaantais tasmin nashte kva vishvataa ..94..
verses.translation_reworded: The Vedanta texts state that ignorance is the material (cause) of the phenomenal world, just as earth is of a jar. Once that (ignorance) is destroyed, where can the universe remain?

verses.sanskrit:
यथा रज्जुं परित्यज्य सर्प गृह्णाति वै भ्रमात्।
तद्वत्सत्यमविज्ञाय जगत्पश्यति मूढधीः।।95।।
verses.roman:
Yathā rajjuṃ parityajya sarpa gṛhṇāti vai bhramāt.
Tadvatsatyamavijñāya jagatpaśyati mūḍhadhīḥ..95..
verses.colloquial:
Yathaa rajjum parityajya sarpa grihnaati vai bhramaat.
Tadvat satyam avijnaaya jagat pashyati muudha dhiih ..95..
verses.translation_reworded: A confused person ignores the rope and perceives only the snake. In the same way, an ignorant person sees only the phenomenal world and does not know the reality.

verses.sanskrit:
रज्जुरूपे परिज्ञाते सर्पभ्रान्तिर्न तिष्ठति।
अधिष्ठाने तथा ज्ञाते प्रपञ्चः शून्यतां व्रजेत्।।96।।
verses.roman:
Rajjurūpe parijñāte sarpabhrāntirna tiṣṭhati.
Adhiṣṭhāne tathā jñāte prapañcaḥ śūnyatāṃ vrajet..96..
verses.colloquial:
Rajjuruupe parijnaate sarpa bhraantir na tishthati.
Adhishthaane tathaa jnaate prapanchah shuunyataam vrajet ..96..
verses.translation_reworded: Once the true nature of the rope is known, the appearance of the snake does not continue. So too, once the substratum is known, the phenomenal world vanishes entirely.

verses.sanskrit:
देहस्यापि प्रपञ्चत्वात्प्रारब्धावस्थितिः कुतः।
अज्ञानिजनबोधार्थं प्रारब्धं वक्ति वै श्रुतिः।।97।।
verses.roman:
Dehasyāpi prapañcatvātprārabdhāvasthitiḥ kutaḥ.
Ajñānijanabodhārthaṃ prārabdhaṃ vakti vai śrutiḥ..97..
verses.colloquial:
Dehasya api prapanchatvaat praarabdha avasthitih kutah.
Ajnaani jana bodhaartham praarabdham vakti vai shrutih ..97..
verses.translation_reworded: Since the body too lies within the phenomenal world (and so is unreal), how could Prarabdha exist? The Shruti speaks of Prarabdha, then, only to help the ignorant understand.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे।
बहुत्वं तन्निषेधार्थं श्रुत्या गीतं च वै स्फुटम्।।98।।
verses.roman:
Kṣīyante cāsya karmāṇi tasmindṛṣṭe parāvare.
Bahutvaṃ tanniṣedhārthaṃ śrutyā gītaṃ ca vai sphuṭam..98..
verses.colloquial:
Kshiiyante cha asya karmaani tasmin drishte paraavare.
Bahutvam tat nishedhaartham shrutyaa giitam cha vai sphutam ..98..
verses.translation_reworded: "And all the actions of a man perish when he realizes that (Atman) which is both the higher and the lower." Here the Shruti's clear use of the plural serves to rule out Prarabdha as well.

verses.sanskrit:
उच्यतेऽज्ञैर्बलाच्चैतत्तदानर्थद्वयागमः।
वेदान्तमतहानं च यतो ज्ञानमिति श्रुतिः।।99।।
verses.roman:
Ucyate'jñairbalāccaitattadānarthadvayāgamaḥ.
Vedāntamatahānaṃ ca yato jñānamiti śrutiḥ..99..
verses.colloquial:
Uchyate'jnair balaat cha etat tad anartha dvaya aagamah.
Vedaanta mata haanam cha yatah jnaanam iti shrutih ..99..
verses.translation_reworded: If the ignorant still insist on this without grounds, they will not only fall into two absurdities but also risk losing the Vedantic conclusion. One should therefore accept only those Shrutis that give rise to true knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
त्रिपञ्चाङ्गान्यथो वक्ष्ये पूर्वोक्तस्यैव सिद्धये।
तैश्च सर्वैः सदा कार्यं निदिध्यासनमेव तु।।100।।
verses.roman:
Tripañcāṅgānyatho vakṣye pūrvoktasyaiva siddhaye.
Taiśca sarvaiḥ sadā kāryaṃ nididhyāsanameva tu..100..
verses.colloquial:
Tripancha angaani atho vakshye puurvoktasya eva siddhaye.
Taih cha sarvaih sadaa kaaryam nididhyaasanam eva tu ..100..
verses.translation_reworded: Now, so that the knowledge just described may be gained, I will explain the fifteen steps with whose help one should practise deep meditation at all times.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्याभ्यासादृते प्राप्तिर्न भवेत्सच्चिदात्मनः।
तस्माद्ब्रह्म निदिध्यासेज्जिज्ञासुः श्रेयसे चिरम्।।101।।
verses.roman:
Nityābhyāsādṛte prāptirna bhavetsaccidātmanaḥ.
Tasmādbrahma nididhyāsejjijñāsuḥ śreyase ciram..101..
verses.colloquial:
Nitya abhyaasaadrite praaptir na bhavet sacchid aatmanah.
Tasmaad brahma nididhyaaset jijnaasuh shreyase chiram ..101..
verses.translation_reworded: The Atman, which is absolute existence and knowledge, cannot be realized without constant practice. So the seeker of knowledge should meditate on Brahman for a long time in order to reach the desired goal.

verses.sanskrit:
यमो हि नियमस्त्यागो मौनं देशश्च कालतः।
आसनं मूलबन्धश्च देहसाम्यं च दृक्स्थितिः।।102।।
verses.roman:
Yamo hi niyamastyāgo maunaṃ deśaśca kālataḥ.
Āsanaṃ mūlabandhaśca dehasāmyaṃ ca dṛksthitiḥ..102..
verses.colloquial:
Yamo hi niyama styaago maunam deshashcha kaalatah.
aasanam muula bandhashcha deha saamyam cha drik sthitih ..102..
verses.translation_reworded: The steps, in sequence, are these: control of the senses, control of the mind, renunciation, silence, space, time, posture, the restraining root (Mulabandha), equipoise of the body, firmness of vision, control of the vital forces, withdrawal of the mind, concentration, self-contemplation, and complete absorption.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राणसंयमनं चैव प्रत्याहारश्च धारणा।
आत्मध्यानं समाधिश्च प्रोक्तान्यङ्गानि वै क्रमात्।।103।।
verses.roman:
Prāṇasaṃyamanaṃ caiva pratyāhāraśca dhāraṇā.
Ātmadhyānaṃ samādhiśca proktānyaṅgāni vai kramāt..103..
verses.colloquial:
Praana samyamanam chaiva pratyaahaarashcha dhaaranaa.
aatma dhyaanam samaadhishcha proktaani angaani vai kramaat ..103..
verses.translation_reworded: The steps, in sequence, are these: control of the senses, control of the mind, renunciation, silence, space, time, posture, the restraining root (Mulabandha), equipoise of the body, firmness of vision, control of the vital forces, withdrawal of the mind, concentration, self-contemplation, and complete absorption.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञानादिन्द्रियग्रामसंयमः।
यमोऽयमिति संप्रोक्तोऽभ्यसनीयो मुहुर्मुहुः।।104।।
verses.roman:
Sarvaṃ brahmeti vijñānādindriyagrāmasaṃyamaḥ.
Yamo'yamiti saṃprokto'bhyasanīyo muhurmuhuḥ..104..
verses.colloquial:
Sarvam brahmeti vijnaanaad indriya graama samyamah.
Yamo'yamiti samprokto'bhyasaniiyo muhurmuhuh ..104..
verses.translation_reworded: Holding back all the senses through such knowledge as "All this is Brahman" is rightly called Yama. It should be practised again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
सजातीयप्रवाहश्च विजातीयतिरस्कृतिः।
नियमो हि परानन्दो नियमात्क्रियते बुधैः।।105।।
verses.roman:
Sajātīyapravāhaśca vijātīyatiraskṛtiḥ.
Niyamo hi parānando niyamātkriyate budhaiḥ..105..
verses.colloquial:
Sajaatiiya pravaahash cha vijaatiiya tiraskritih.
Niyamo hi paraanando niyamaat kriyate budhaih ..105..
verses.translation_reworded: A continuous stream of a single kind of thought, with every other thought excluded, is called Niyama. It is the supreme bliss indeed, and the wise practise it regularly.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यागः प्रपञ्चरूपस्य चिदात्मत्वावलोकनात्।
त्यागो हि महतां पूज्यः सद्यो मोक्षमयो यतः।।106।।
verses.roman:
Tyāgaḥ prapañcarūpasya cidātmatvāvalokanāt.
Tyāgo hi mahatāṃ pūjyaḥ sadyo mokṣamayo yataḥ..106..
verses.colloquial:
Tyaagah prapancha ruupasya chidaatmatva avalokanaat.
Tyaagah hi mahataam puujyah sadyo moksha mayo yatah ..106..
verses.translation_reworded: To give up the illusory universe by realizing it as the all-conscious Atman is the true renunciation. The great honour it because it is immediate liberation by nature.

verses.sanskrit:
यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह।
यन्मौनं योगिभिर्गम्यं तद्भजेत्सर्वदा बुधः।।107।।
verses.roman:
Yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha.
Yanmaunaṃ yogibhirgamyaṃ tadbhajetsarvadā budhaḥ..107..
verses.colloquial:
Yato vaacho nivartante apraapya manasaa saha.
Yanmaunam yogibhir gamyam tadbhajet sarvadaa budhah ..107..
verses.translation_reworded: The wise should always be one with that silence which words and the mind turn back from without reaching, but which Yogins can attain.

verses.sanskrit:
वाचो यस्मान्निवर्तन्ते तद्वक्तुं केन शक्यते।
प्रपञ्चो यदि वक्तव्यः सोऽपि शब्दविवर्जितः।।108।।
verses.roman:
Vāco yasmānnivartante tadvaktuṃ kena śakyate.
Prapañco yadi vaktavyaḥ so'pi śabdavivarjitaḥ..108..
verses.colloquial:
Vaacho yasmaan nivartante tad vaktum kena shakyate.
Prapancho yadi vaktavyah so'pi shabda vivarjitah ..108..
verses.translation_reworded: Who can describe That (Brahman) from which words turn away? (So silence is unavoidable in describing Brahman.) And if one tried to describe the phenomenal world, that too is beyond words. This, as an alternative definition, may also be called silence, known among the sages as congenital. Keeping silent by holding back speech, on the other hand, is prescribed by the teachers of Brahman for the ignorant.

verses.sanskrit:
इति वा तद्भवेन्मौनं सतां सहजसंज्ञितम्।
गिरा मौनं तु बालानां प्रयुक्तं ब्रह्मवादिभिः।।109।।
verses.roman:
Iti vā tadbhavenmaunaṃ satāṃ sahajasaṃjñitam.
Girā maunaṃ tu bālānāṃ prayuktaṃ brahmavādibhiḥ..109..
verses.colloquial:
Iti vaa tadbhavet maunam sataam sahaja samjnitam.
Giraa maunam tu baalaanaam prayuktam brahma vaadibhih ..109..
verses.translation_reworded: Who can describe That (Brahman) from which words turn away? (So silence is unavoidable in describing Brahman.) And if one tried to describe the phenomenal world, that too is beyond words. This, as an alternative definition, may also be called silence, known among the sages as congenital. Keeping silent by holding back speech, on the other hand, is prescribed by the teachers of Brahman for the ignorant.

verses.sanskrit:
आदावन्ते च मध्ये च जनो यस्मिन्न विद्यते।
येनेदं सततं व्याप्तं स देशो विजनः स्मृतः।।110।।
verses.roman:
Ādāvante ca madhye ca jano yasminna vidyate.
Yenedaṃ satataṃ vyāptaṃ sa deśo vijanaḥ smṛtaḥ..110..
verses.colloquial:
aadau ante cha madhye cha jano yasmin na vidyate.
Yena idam satatam vyaaptam sa desho vijanah smritah ..110..
verses.translation_reworded: "Space" means that solitude in which the universe does not exist at the beginning, the end, or the middle, yet by which it is pervaded at all times.

verses.sanskrit:
कलनात्सर्वभूतानां ब्रह्मादीनां निमेषतः।
कालशब्देन निर्दिष्टो ह्यखण्डानन्द अद्वयः।।111।।
verses.roman:
Kalanātsarvabhūtānāṃ brahmādīnāṃ nimeṣataḥ.
Kālaśabdena nirdiṣṭo hyakhaṇḍānanda advayaḥ..111..
verses.colloquial:
Kalanaat sarvabhuutaanaam brahmaadiinaam nimeshatah.
Kaalashabdena nirdishto hyakhandaananda advayah ..111..
verses.translation_reworded: The non-dual (Brahman), which is undivided bliss, is what the word "time" refers to, since in the blink of an eye it brings into being all creatures from Brahman downward.

verses.sanskrit:
सुखेनैव भवेद्यस्मिन्नजस्रं ब्रह्मचिन्तनम्।
आसनं तद्विजानीयान्नेतरत्सुखनाशनम्।।112।।
verses.roman:
Sukhenaiva bhavedyasminnajasraṃ brahmacintanam.
Āsanaṃ tadvijānīyānnetaratsukhanāśanam..112..
verses.colloquial:
Sukhenaiva bhaved yasminnajasram brahma chintanam.
aasanam tad vijaaniiyaan netarat sukha naashanam ..112..
verses.translation_reworded: Know that the true posture is the one in which meditation on Brahman flows on its own without a break, and not any other that destroys one's happiness.

verses.sanskrit:
सिद्धं यत्सर्वभूतादि विश्वाधिष्ठानमव्ययम्।
यस्मिन्सिद्धाः समाविष्टास्तद्वै सिद्धासनं विदुः।।113।।
verses.roman:
Siddhaṃ yatsarvabhūtādi viśvādhiṣṭhānamavyayam.
Yasminsiddhāḥ samāviṣṭāstadvai siddhāsanaṃ viduḥ..113..
verses.colloquial:
Siddham yat sarvabhuutaadi vishvaadhishthaanam avyayam.
Yasmin siddhaah samaavishtaas tad vai siddhaasanam viduh ..113..
verses.translation_reworded: That which is well known as the origin of all beings and the support of the whole universe, which does not change, and in which the enlightened are fully merged: that alone is known as Siddhasana (eternal Brahman).

verses.sanskrit:
यन्मूलं सर्वभूतानां यन्मूलं चित्तबन्धनम्।
मूलबन्धः सदा सेव्यो योगोऽसौ राजयोगिनाम्।।114।।
verses.roman:
Yanmūlaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ yanmūlaṃ cittabandhanam.
Mūlabandhaḥ sadā sevyo yogo'sau rājayoginām..114..
verses.colloquial:
Yan muulam sarva bhuutaanaam yan muulam chitta bandhanam.
Muula bandhah sadaa sevyo yogo'sau raaja yoginaam ..114..
verses.translation_reworded: That (Brahman) which is the root of all existence, and on which restraint of the mind rests, is called the restraining root (Mulabandha). It should always be adopted, since it is fit for Raja-yogins.

verses.sanskrit:
अङ्गानां समतां विद्यात्समे ब्रह्मणि लीयते।
नो चेन्नैव समानत्वमृजुत्वं शुष्कवृक्षवत्।।115।।
verses.roman:
Aṅgānāṃ samatāṃ vidyātsame brahmaṇi līyate.
No cennaiva samānatvamṛjutvaṃ śuṣkavṛkṣavat..115..
verses.colloquial:
Angaanaam samataam vidyaat same brahmani liiyate.
Nah chet na eva samaanatvam rijutvam shushka vrikshavat ..115..
verses.translation_reworded: Absorption in the uniform Brahman should be understood as the equipoise of the limbs (Dehasamya). Merely holding the body straight, like a dried-up tree, is not equipoise.

verses.sanskrit:
दृष्टिं ज्ञानमयीं कृत्वा पश्येद्ब्रह्ममयं जगत्।
सा दृष्टिः परमोदारा न नासाग्रावलोकनी।।116।।
verses.roman:
Dṛṣṭiṃ jñānamayīṃ kṛtvā paśyedbrahmamayaṃ jagat.
Sā dṛṣṭiḥ paramodārā na nāsāgrāvalokanī..116..
verses.colloquial:
Drishtim jnaana mayiim kritvaa pashyet brahma mayam jagat.
Saa drishtih parama udaaraa na naasaagraavalokanii ..116..
verses.translation_reworded: Turning ordinary sight into the sight of knowledge, one should see the world as Brahman itself. That is the noblest vision, not the one aimed at the tip of the nose.

verses.sanskrit:
द्रष्टृदर्शनदृश्यानां विरामो यत्र वा भवेत्।
दृष्टिस्तत्रैव कर्तव्या न नासाग्रावलोकनी।।117।।
verses.roman:
Draṣṭṛdarśanadṛśyānāṃ virāmo yatra vā bhavet.
Dṛṣṭistatraiva kartavyā na nāsāgrāvalokanī..117..
verses.colloquial:
Drashtri darshana drishyaanaam viraamo yatra vaa bhavet.
Drishtis tatraiva kartavyaa na naasaagraavalokanii ..117..
verses.translation_reworded: Or one should turn one's vision only to That in which every distinction of seer, sight, and seen comes to an end, and not to the tip of the nose.

verses.sanskrit:
चित्तादिसर्वभावेषु ब्रह्मत्वेनैव भावनात्।
निरोधः सर्ववृत्तीनां प्राणायामः स उच्यते।।118।।
verses.roman:
Cittādisarvabhāveṣu brahmatvenaiva bhāvanāt.
Nirodhaḥ sarvavṛttīnāṃ prāṇāyāmaḥ sa ucyate..118..
verses.colloquial:
Chitta aadi sarva bhaaveshu brahmatvena eva bhaavanaat.
Nirodhah sarva vrittiinaam praanaayaamah sa uchyate ..118..
verses.translation_reworded: Restraining all modifications of the mind by regarding every mental state, such as the Chitta, as Brahman alone is called Pranayama.

verses.sanskrit:
निषेधनं प्रपञ्चस्य रेचकाख्यः समीरणः।
ब्रह्मैवास्मीति या वृत्तिः पूरको वायुरीरितः।।119।।
verses.roman:
Niṣedhanaṃ prapañcasya recakākhyaḥ samīraṇaḥ.
Brahmaivāsmīti yā vṛttiḥ pūrako vāyurīritaḥ..119..
verses.colloquial:
Nishedhanam prapanchasya rechaka aakhyh samiiranah.
Brahma eva asmi iti yaa vrittih puurakah vaayuh iiritah ..119..
verses.translation_reworded: Denying the phenomenal world is known as Rechaka (breathing out). The thought "I am truly Brahman" is called Puraka (breathing in). Holding steadily to that thought afterwards is called Kumbhaka (restraining the breath). This is the real Pranayama for the enlightened, while the ignorant merely torture the nose.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तद्वृत्तिनैश्चल्यं कुम्भकः प्राणसंयमः।
अयं चापि प्रबुद्धानामज्ञानां घ्राणपीडनम्।।120।।
verses.roman:
Tatastadvṛttinaiścalyaṃ kumbhakaḥ prāṇasaṃyamaḥ.
Ayaṃ cāpi prabuddhānāmajñānāṃ ghrāṇapīḍanam..120..
verses.colloquial:
Tatas tad vritti naishchalyam kumbhakah praana samyamah.
Ayam cha api prabuddhaanaam ajnaanaam ghraana piidanam ..120..
verses.translation_reworded: Denying the phenomenal world is known as Rechaka (breathing out). The thought "I am truly Brahman" is called Puraka (breathing in). Holding steadily to that thought afterwards is called Kumbhaka (restraining the breath). This is the real Pranayama for the enlightened, while the ignorant merely torture the nose.

verses.sanskrit:
विषयेष्वात्मतां दृष्ट्वा मनसश्चिति मज्जनम्।
प्रत्याहारः स विज्ञेयोऽभ्यसनीयो मुमुक्षुभिः।।121।।
verses.roman:
Viṣayeṣvātmatāṃ dṛṣṭvā manasaściti majjanam.
Pratyāhāraḥ sa vijñeyo'bhyasanīyo mumukṣubhiḥ..121..
verses.colloquial:
Vishayeshu aatmataam drishtvaa manasah chiti majjanam.
Pratyaahaarah sa vijneyah abhyasaniiyah mumukshubhih ..121..
verses.translation_reworded: When the mind sinks into the Supreme Consciousness by recognizing Atman in every object, that is called Pratyahara (withdrawal of the mind). Those who seek liberation should practice it.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र यत्र मनो याति ब्रह्मणस्तत्र दर्शनात्।
मनसो धारणायैव धारणा सा परा मता।।122।।
verses.roman:
Yatra yatra mano yāti brahmaṇastatra darśanāt.
Manaso dhāraṇāyaiva dhāraṇā sā parā matā..122..
verses.colloquial:
Yatra yatra mano yaati brahmanas tatra darshanaat.
Manaso dhaaranaayaiva dhaaranaa saa paraa mataa ..122..
verses.translation_reworded: Holding the mind steady by recognizing Brahman wherever the mind travels is called the highest Dharana (concentration).

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मैवास्मीति सद्वृत्त्या निरालम्बतया स्थितिः।
ध्यानशब्देन विख्याता परमानन्ददायिनी।।123।।
verses.roman:
Brahmaivāsmīti sadvṛttyā nirālambatayā sthitiḥ.
Dhyānaśabdena vikhyātā paramānandadāyinī..123..
verses.colloquial:
Brahma eva asmi iti sadvrittyaa niraalambatayaa sthitih.
Dhyaana shabdena vikhyaataa parama aananda daayinii ..123..
verses.translation_reworded: Standing free of everything, grounded in the unshakable conviction 'I am indeed Brahman,' is what the word Dhyana (meditation) refers to. It yields the highest bliss.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्विकारतया वृत्त्या ब्रह्माकारतया पुनः।
वृत्तिविस्मरणं सम्यक्समाधिर्ज्ञानसंज्ञकः।।124।।
verses.roman:
Nirvikāratayā vṛttyā brahmākāratayā punaḥ.
Vṛttivismaraṇaṃ samyaksamādhirjñānasaṃjñakaḥ..124..
verses.colloquial:
Nirvikaaratayaa vrittyaa brahmaakaaratayaa punah.
Vritti vismaranam samyak samaadhih jnaana samjnakah ..124..
verses.translation_reworded: Making thought first unmoving, then identifying it with Brahman, and so forgetting all thought entirely, is called Samadhi. It is also called knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं चाकृत्रिमानन्दं तावत्साधु समभ्यसेत्।
वश्यो यावत्क्षणात्पुंसः प्रयुक्तः स भेवत्स्वयम्।।125।।
verses.roman:
Evaṃ cākṛtrimānandaṃ tāvatsādhu samabhyaset.
Vaśyo yāvatkṣaṇātpuṃsaḥ prayuktaḥ sa bhevatsvayam..125..
verses.colloquial:
Evam chaakritrima aanandam taavat saadhu samabhyaset.
Vashyah yaavat kshanaat pumsah prayuktah sa bhavet svayam ..125..
verses.translation_reworded: The seeker should diligently practice this meditation, which uncovers his innate bliss, until it comes fully under his command and springs up on its own the instant it is summoned.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः साधननिर्मुक्तः सिद्धो भवति योगिराट्।
तत्स्वरूपं न चैकस्य विषयो मनसो गिराम्।।126।।
verses.roman:
Tataḥ sādhananirmuktaḥ siddho bhavati yogirāṭ.
Tatsvarūpaṃ na caikasya viṣayo manaso girām..126..
verses.colloquial:
Tatah saadhana nirmuktah siddho bhavati yogiraat.
Tat svaruupam na chaikasya vishayo manaso giraam ..126..
verses.translation_reworded: Then this foremost of Yogis, having reached perfection, is released from all practice. The true nature of such a person can never be grasped by mind or by speech.

verses.sanskrit:
समाधौ क्रियमाणे तु विघ्ना आयान्ति वै बलात्।
अनुसंधानराहित्यमालस्यं भोगलालसम्।।127।।
verses.roman:
Samādhau kriyamāṇe tu vighnā āyānti vai balāt.
Anusaṃdhānarāhityamālasyaṃ bhogalālasam..127..
verses.colloquial:
Samaadhau kriyamaane tu vighnaa aayaanti vai balaat.
Anusamdhaana raahityam aalasyam bhoga laalasam ..127..
verses.translation_reworded: During the practice of Samadhi many obstacles inevitably appear: failure to inquire, laziness, craving for sense pleasure, sleep, dullness, distraction, savoring of joy, and a sense of emptiness. Whoever wants knowledge of Brahman should gradually remove these countless obstacles.

verses.sanskrit:
लयस्तमश्च विक्षेपो रसास्वादश्च शून्यता।
एवं यद्विघ्नबाहुल्यं त्याज्यं ब्रह्मविदा शनैः।।128।।
verses.roman:
Layastamaśca vikṣepo rasāsvādaśca śūnyatā.
Evaṃ yadvighnabāhulyaṃ tyājyaṃ brahmavidā śanaiḥ..128..
verses.colloquial:
Layas tamash cha vikshepo rasaasvaadash cha shuunyataa.
Evam yad vighna baahulyam tyaajyam brahmavidaa shanaih ..128..
verses.translation_reworded: During the practice of Samadhi many obstacles inevitably appear: failure to inquire, laziness, craving for sense pleasure, sleep, dullness, distraction, savoring of joy, and a sense of emptiness. Whoever wants knowledge of Brahman should gradually remove these countless obstacles.

verses.sanskrit:
भाववृत्त्या हि भावत्वं शून्यवृत्त्या हि शून्यता।
ब्रह्मवृत्त्या हि पूर्णत्वं तथा पूर्णत्वमभ्यसेत्।।129।।
verses.roman:
Bhāvavṛttyā hi bhāvatvaṃ śūnyavṛttyā hi śūnyatā.
Brahmavṛttyā hi pūrṇatvaṃ tathā pūrṇatvamabhyaset..129..
verses.colloquial:
Bhaava vrittyaa hi bhaavatvam shuunya vrittyaa hi shuunyataa.
Brahma vrittyaa hi puurnatvam tathaa puurnatvam abhyaset ..129..
verses.translation_reworded: When the mind dwells on an object it truly becomes one with that object; when it dwells on a void it truly becomes blank; but when it dwells on Brahman it reaches perfection. So one should think of Brahman constantly in order to reach perfection.

verses.sanskrit:
ये हि वृत्तिं जहत्येनां ब्रह्माख्यां पावनीं पराम्।
वृथैव ते तु जीवन्ति पशुभिश्च समा नराः।।130।।
verses.roman:
Ye hi vṛttiṃ jahatyenāṃ brahmākhyāṃ pāvanīṃ parām.
Vṛthaiva te tu jīvanti paśubhiśca samā narāḥ..130..
verses.colloquial:
Ye hi vrittim jahati enaam brahmaakhyaam paavaniim paraam.
Vrithaiva te tu jiivanti pashubhish cha samaa naraah ..130..
verses.translation_reworded: Those who abandon this supremely purifying thought of Brahman live for nothing and stand on the same level as animals.

verses.sanskrit:
ये हि वृत्तिं विजानन्ति ये ज्ञात्वा वर्धयन्त्यपि।
ते वै सत्पुरुषा धन्या वन्द्यास्ते भुवनत्रये।।131।।
verses.roman:
Ye hi vṛttiṃ vijānanti ye jñātvā vardhayantyapi.
Te vai satpuruṣā dhanyā vandyāste bhuvanatraye..131..
verses.colloquial:
Ye hi vrittim vijaananti ye jnaatvaa vardhayanti api.
Te vai satpurushaa dhanyaa vandyaas te bhuvana traye ..131..
verses.translation_reworded: Truly fortunate are the virtuous people who first gain this awareness of Brahman and then cultivate it further and further. They are honored wherever they go.

verses.sanskrit:
येषां वृत्तिः समावृद्धा परिपक्वा च सा पुनः।
ते वै सद्ब्रह्मतां प्राप्ता नेतरे शब्दवादिनः।।132।।
verses.roman:
Yeṣāṃ vṛttiḥ samāvṛddhā paripakvā ca sā punaḥ.
Te vai sadbrahmatāṃ prāptā netare śabdavādinaḥ..132..
verses.colloquial:
Yeshaam vrittih samaavriddhaa paripakvaa cha saa punah.
Te vai sadbrahmataam praaptaa netare shabda vaadinah ..132..
verses.translation_reworded: Only those in whom this ever-present awareness of Brahman ripens into maturity reach the state of the eternally existing Brahman. Those who merely traffic in words do not.

verses.sanskrit:
कुशला ब्रह्मवार्तायां वृत्तिहीनाः सुरागिणः।
तेऽप्यज्ञानितमा नूनं पुनरायान्ति यान्ति च।।133।।
verses.roman:
Kuśalā brahmavārtāyāṃ vṛttihīnāḥ surāgiṇaḥ.
Te'pyajñānitamā nūnaṃ punarāyānti yānti ca..133..
verses.colloquial:
Kushalaa brahma vaartaayaam vritti hiinaah suraaginah.
Te'pi ajnaanitamaa nuunam punah aayaanti yaanti cha ..133..
verses.translation_reworded: Likewise, people who are skilled only at talking about Brahman, who have no realization and remain deeply attached to worldly pleasures, are born and die over and over because of their ignorance.

verses.sanskrit:
निमेषार्धं न तिष्ठन्ति वृत्तिं ब्रह्ममयीं विना।
यथा तिष्ठन्ति ब्रह्माद्याः सनकाद्याः शुकादयः।।134।।
verses.roman:
Nimeṣārdhaṃ na tiṣṭhanti vṛttiṃ brahmamayīṃ vinā.
Yathā tiṣṭhanti brahmādyāḥ sanakādyāḥ śukādayaḥ..134..
verses.colloquial:
Nimeshaardham na tishthanti vrittim brahmamayiim vinaa.
Yathaa tishthanti brahma aadyaah sanaka aadyaah shuka aadayah ..134..
verses.translation_reworded: Those who seek Brahman should not pass a single moment without the thought of Brahman, following the example of Brahma, Sanaka, Suka, and others.

verses.sanskrit:
कार्ये कारणतायाता कारणे न हि कार्यता।
कारणत्वं स्वतो गच्छेत्कार्याभावे विचारतः।।135।।
verses.roman:
Kārye kāraṇatāyātā kāraṇe na hi kāryatā.
Kāraṇatvaṃ svato gacchetkāryābhāve vicārataḥ..135..
verses.colloquial:
Kaarye kaarana taa yaataa kaarane na hi kaaryataa.
Kaaranatvam svato gacchet kaarya abhaave vichaaratah ..135..
verses.translation_reworded: The nature of the cause is present in the effect, but not the other way around. Reasoning therefore shows that when the effect is absent, the cause as such disappears too.

verses.sanskrit:
अथ शुद्धं भवेद्वस्तु यद्वै वाचामगोचरः।
द्रष्टव्यं मृद्धटेनैव दृष्टान्तेन पुनः पुनः।।136।।
verses.roman:
Atha śuddhaṃ bhavedvastu yadvai vācāmagocaraḥ.
Draṣṭavyaṃ mṛddhaṭenaiva dṛṣṭāntena punaḥ punaḥ..136..
verses.colloquial:
Atha shuddham bhavet vastu yad vai vaachaam agocharah.
Drashtavyam mrid dhatena eva drishtaantena punah punah ..136..
verses.translation_reworded: What then remains is only that pure reality, Brahman, which lies beyond speech. This should be grasped again and again through the example of the clay and the pot.

verses.sanskrit:
अनेनैव प्रकारेण वृत्तिर्ब्रह्मात्मिका भवेत्।
उदेति शुद्धचित्तानां वृत्तिज्ञानं ततः परम्।।137।।
verses.roman:
Anenaiva prakāreṇa vṛttirbrahmātmikā bhavet.
Udeti śuddhacittānāṃ vṛttijñānaṃ tataḥ param..137..
verses.colloquial:
Anenaiva prakaarena vrittir brahmaatmikaa bhavet.
Udeti shuddha chittaanaam vritti jnaanam tatah param ..137..
verses.translation_reworded: By this path alone does an awareness of Brahman dawn in the pure-minded, an awareness that is afterwards absorbed into Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
कारणं व्यतिरेकेण पुमानादौ विलोकयेत्।
अन्वयेन पुनस्तद्धि कार्ये नित्यं प्रपश्यति।।138।।
verses.roman:
Kāraṇaṃ vyatirekeṇa pumānādau vilokayet.
Anvayena punastaddhi kārye nityaṃ prapaśyati..138..
verses.colloquial:
Kaaranam vyatirekena pumaan aadau vilokayet.
Anvayena punas taddhi kaarye nityam prapashyati ..138..
verses.translation_reworded: One should first seek the cause by the method of negation, and then discover it by the positive method as something always present within the effect.

verses.sanskrit:
कार्ये हि कारणं पश्येत्पश्चात्कार्यं विसर्जयेत्।
कारणत्वं स्वतो नश्येदवशिष्टं भवेन्मुनिः।।139।।
verses.roman:
Kārye hi kāraṇaṃ paśyetpaścātkāryaṃ visarjayet.
Kāraṇatvaṃ svato naśyedavaśiṣṭaṃ bhavenmuniḥ..139..
verses.colloquial:
Kaarye hi kaaranam pashyet pashchaat kaaryam visarjayet.
Kaarana tvam svato nashyet avashishtam bhavet munih ..139..
verses.translation_reworded: One should truly see the cause within the effect, and then set the effect aside completely. Whatever remains, the sage himself becomes.

verses.sanskrit:
भावितं तीव्रवेगेण वस्तु यन्निश्चयात्मना।
पुमांस्तद्धि भवेच्छीघ्रं ज्ञेयं भ्रमरकीटवत्।।140।।
verses.roman:
Bhāvitaṃ tīvravegeṇa vastu yanniścayātmanā.
Pumāṃstaddhi bhavecchīghraṃ jñeyaṃ bhramarakīṭavat..140..
verses.colloquial:
Bhaavitam tiivravegena vastu yan nishchayaatmanaa.
Pumaams taddhi bhavet shiighram jneyam bhramara kiitavat ..140..
verses.translation_reworded: A person who meditates on something with intense effort and firm conviction turns into that very thing. The example of the wasp and the worm makes this clear.

verses.sanskrit:
अदृश्यं भावरूपं च सर्वमेतच्चिदात्मकम्।
सावधानतया नित्यं स्वात्मानं भावयेद्बुधः।।141।।
verses.roman:
Adṛśyaṃ bhāvarūpaṃ ca sarvametaccidātmakam.
Sāvadhānatayā nityaṃ svātmānaṃ bhāvayedbudhaḥ..141..
verses.colloquial:
Adrishyam bhaavaruupam cha sarvam etac chidaatmakam.
Saavadhaanatayaa nityam svaatmaanam bhaavayed budhah ..141..
verses.translation_reworded: The wise person should always, with great care, regard the unseen, the seen, and everything else as his own Self, which is consciousness itself.

verses.sanskrit:
दृश्यं ह्यदृश्यतां नीत्वा ब्रह्माकारेण चिन्तयेत्।
विद्वान्नित्यसुखे तिष्ठेद्धिया चिद्रसपूर्णया।।142।।
verses.roman:
Dṛśyaṃ hyadṛśyatāṃ nītvā brahmākāreṇa cintayet.
Vidvānnityasukhe tiṣṭheddhiyā cidrasapūrṇayā..142..
verses.colloquial:
Drishyam hyadrishyataam niitvaa brahmaakaarena chintayet.
Vidvaan nitya sukhe tishthed dhiyaa chid rasa puurnayaa ..142..
verses.translation_reworded: Having resolved the visible into the invisible, the wise person should regard the universe as one with Brahman. Only in this way will he rest in everlasting happiness, his mind filled with consciousness and bliss.

verses.sanskrit:
एभिरङ्गैः समायुक्तो राजयोग उदाहृतः।
किंचित्पक्वकषायाणां हठयोगेन संयुतः।।143।।
verses.roman:
Ebhiraṅgaiḥ samāyukto rājayoga udāhṛtaḥ.
Kiṃcitpakvakaṣāyāṇāṃ haṭhayogena saṃyutaḥ..143..
verses.colloquial:
Ebhir angaih samaayukto raaja yoga udaahritah.
Kimchit pakva kashaayaanaam hatha yogena samyutah ..143..
verses.translation_reworded: This completes the description of Raja-Yoga with the steps given above. For those whose worldly desires are only partly worn down, Hatha-Yoga should be combined with it.

verses.sanskrit:
परिपक्वं मनो येषां केवलोऽयं च सिद्धिदः।
गुरुदैवतभक्तानां सर्वेषां सुलभो जवात्।।144।।
verses.roman:
Paripakvaṃ mano yeṣāṃ kevalo'yaṃ ca siddhidaḥ.
Gurudaivatabhaktānāṃ sarveṣāṃ sulabho javāt..144..
verses.colloquial:
Paripakvam mano yeshaam kevalo'yam cha siddhidah.
Guru daivata bhaktaanaam sarveshaam sulabho javaat ..144..
verses.translation_reworded: For those whose minds are wholly purified, Raja-Yoga by itself brings perfection. And purity of mind comes quickly to those devoted to the teacher and to the Deity.

verses.sanskrit:
इति श्रीमत्परमहंसपरिव्राजकाचार्यस्य
श्रीगोविन्दभगवत्पूज्यपादशिष्यस्य
श्रीमच्छंकरभगवतः कृतौ
अपरोक्षानुभूतिः समाप्ता।।
verses.roman:
Iti śrīmatparamahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya
Śrīgovindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya
Śrīmacchaṃkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau
Aparokṣānubhūtiḥ samāptā..
verses.colloquial:
Iti shriimat parama hamsa parivraajaka aachaaryasya
shrii govinda bhagavat puujya paada shishyasya
shriimat shamkara bhagavatah kritau
Aparoksha anubhuutih samaaptaa..
verses.translation_reworded: Thus concludes the Aparokshanubhuti, the work of the revered Shankaracharya, a supreme ascetic and wandering monk who was the disciple of the venerable Govindapada. [Not verified]
